newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines sees tentative pact by weekend.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines sees tentative pact by weekend.

text.p: American Airlines said Tuesday that federally mediated labour negotiations with its pilots union have been "productive" and it expected a tentative settlement by the end of the week.
American, a unit of AMR Corp., said the tentative settlement would be presented to the board of the Allied Pilots Association at a meeting Friday in Washington.
The nation's No. 2 airline and its pilots union resumed talks last Friday for the first time since a week of intensive negotiations broke down without an agreement Feb. 14.

The 9,300-member union went on strike just after midnight Feb. 15 but President Clinton immediately created an emergency board to try to resolve the dispute over wages and whether American will use APA pilots or other pilots to fly new small commuter jets for its regional carrier, American Eagle.

Under federal labour law governing airlines, Clinton's action stopped the pilots from striking and stopped American from locking the pilots out for 60 days while a mediation board drew up a proposed settlement and the two sides considered it.
On Monday the White House said American and the union had agreed to extend the 60-day period to April 28, two weeks beyond the original deadline.
If a voluntary solution is not reached by April 28, the pilots could strike or American could lock them out.
